cases.prompt: The requirement for hourly downtime by reason at our press line is accepted. Write the epic and split it into stories we can put in the backlog. (fictional plant)
cases.expected_output: Writes a background with today, role and hour, the moment of use, the decision it changes, why now and what it is not for. Writes an epic statement with a named role and a plant-specific outcome. Cuts at least two stories by moment and role, not by technical layer. Each story has Given/When/Then including a real-shift criterion. Runs the epic check and fixes blockers before handover.

cases.prompt: Our stories are: 1 connect the PLC, 2 build the flow, 3 build the dashboard. Is that a good epic breakdown?
cases.expected_output: Says this is a task plan, not stories, because none is usable or acceptable alone. Proposes cutting by moment and role or by signal availability. Does not hand the breakdown over.

cases.prompt: The epic says 'so that we get more transparency and faster reaction'. Can this go into the backlog?
cases.expected_output: Flags the sentence as generic and fitting any plant's epic. Asks for the role, the decision it changes and the plant-specific outcome. Suggests running the epic check. Does not invent the outcome.

cases.prompt: The plant only told us they want 'something with OEE'. Turn this into signals and testable acceptance criteria.
cases.expected_output: Recognises this as requirement derivation that comes before epics. Points to the requirements skill instead of writing an epic.

should_trigger: Write the epic and user stories for this accepted requirement
Check this epic before it goes into the backlog
How should we split this epic into stories that stand alone?
Our user stories all share the same so-that sentence, fix them
should_not_trigger: Derive the signals and acceptance criteria from this plant demand
Calculate the savings and payback of this use case
Build a click-dummy to prove the idea
Write the acceptance test protocol for the delivered connection
